articles.title: OpenWorld (NASDAQ: OPNW) Signs Definitive Merger Agreement to Acquire Blocksight
articles.description: OpenWorld (NASDAQ: OPNW) Signs Definitive Merger Agreement to Acquire Blocksight as the Agentic Foundation for Its Up to $1 Billion Tokenized Solar and AI Computing Program with Meridian and Up to $130 Million IP-Backed Transaction with BeyondAI. Blocksight's AI agents are expected to handle deal structuring, asset verification, investor onboarding and daily reporting across more than $1.1 billion in recently announced tokenized financing programs on the OpenWorld Enterprise platform LAKE MARY, Fla., Oct. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- OpenWorld, Inc. ("OpenWorld” or the "Company”) (NASDAQ: OPNW), an innovation company advancing global real-world asset ("RWA”) tokenization, today announced the signing of a definitive merger agreement to acquire Blocksight and outlined how its acquisition of Blocksight Holdings Co. ("Blocksight”), announced on October 1, 2026, is intended to serve as the operating foundation for the Company’s tokenized financing programs in infrastructure and energy. Blocksight builds AI agents that bring real-world assets on-chain, automating deal structuring, asset data verification, investor onboarding, daily investor reporting and ongoing investment servicing, with human approval required at key decision points. Upon completion of the acquisition, these agents are expected to be integrated into OpenWorld Enterprise, the platform through which OpenWorld structures, administers and reports on tokenized RWA programs. In the two weeks since the Blocksight announcement, OpenWorld has announced two tokenized financing programs that OpenWorld Enterprise is expected to structure and service. On October 7, 2026, the Company entered into a non-binding term sheet with BeyondAI for a proposed intellectual property-backed transaction of up to $130 million, under which digital tokens would represent investors’ rights to payments backed by eligible BeyondAI intellectual property. On October 15, 2026, the Company entered into a non-binding term sheet with Meridian to establish a tokenized financing program of up to $1 billion to fund a distributed AI computing network powered by on-site solar energy and residential battery storage, with an expected initial deployment planned for 10,000 homes. Together, the three announcements describe a single model: one platform, one agentic workflow, applied across asset classes. Key Highlights One platform, one repeatable model: OpenWorld Enterprise is the structuring, administration and reporting layer for each program. Blocksight’s agents are intended to become the orchestration layer inside that platform, so that each new program reuses the same verification, onboarding and reporting infrastructure rather than rebuilding it. Agentic workflow with human approval: Blocksight’s agents are expected to cover five stages of a tokenized financing: deal structuring, asset data verification, investor onboarding, daily investor reporting and ongoing servicing. People approve the decisions that matter at each stage. Applied to intellectual property (BeyondAI): In an IP-backed structure, the agents are expected to verify eligible patents and software rights, onboard investors and report daily on the payment streams that back the tokens, while BeyondAI retains control of its technology. Applied to energy and computing infrastructure (Meridian): In a distributed network of residential battery storage, solar panels and AI computing equipment across thousands of properties, the agents are expected to ingest equipment performance data via IOT devices, reconcile hosting payments and AI inference revenue, and deliver investor reporting on the underlying assets. Team: The Blocksight co-founders Patrick Kim and Peter Hong are expected to join OpenWorld upon closing of the merger. "We want to build a model in which the Blocksight acquisition provides the foundation for our tokenization work in infrastructure and energy,” said Matt Shaw, CEO of OpenWorld. "We expect our proposed transaction with BeyondAI to demonstrate that industrial AI intellectual property can be structured as financeable collateral. Our term sheet with Meridian extends that same model to physical assets: Tesla Powerwall residential battery storage, solar generation and AI compute nodes across thousands of properties. Programs of that size cannot be verified, onboarded and reported on by hand. Blocksight’s agents are how we intend to do it at scale, with people approving every decision that matters.” From Transaction to Platform Tokenizing a real-world asset is not a single event. Each program requires the underlying assets to be structured into a financeable form, the data behind those assets to be verified, investors to be onboarded and documented, performance to be reported on a continuing basis, and payments to be serviced over the life of the structure. Performed manually, each of these steps limits how many programs a platform can run and how large each program can be. Blocksight was built to automate that lifecycle. Its agents structure deals, verify asset data, onboard investors, produce daily investor reporting and service investments on an ongoing basis, with humans required for key decisions. After the closing of the merger, OpenWorld intends to make this workflow the standard operating layer of OpenWorld Enterprise, so that the Company can take on larger programs, across more asset classes, with consistent verification and reporting for investors. Applying the Model: BeyondAI Under the October 7, 2026 term sheet, OpenWorld would provide transaction structuring, tokenization, technology integration, reporting infrastructure and operational services for a proposed IP-backed transaction of up to $130 million. Each token would represent an investor’s rights to payments backed by eligible BeyondAI intellectual property, such as patents and software rights. The proposed arrangement is a financing backed by IP rights, not a sale of BeyondAI’s technology, and BeyondAI would retain control of its technology. Within this structure, Blocksight’s agents are expected to support the verification of eligible intellectual property, the onboarding of investors and the daily reporting on the payment streams that back the tokens. Applying the Model: Meridian Under the October 15, 2026 term sheet, OpenWorld would serve as advisor, structuring agent and services provider for a tokenized financing program of up to $1 billion, and OpenWorld Enterprise would finance and operate the orchestration of a distributed AI computing network. Meridian holds purchase rights to Tesla Powerwall residential battery storage systems for the program and would own the storage assets within the structure. Residential battery storage, solar panels and AI computing equipment form the asset base. The initial deployment is planned for 10,000 homes, with larger installations at local schools, hospitals and commercial campuses. Initial installations are scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026, with the first commercial site targeted for the first quarter of 2027. A program of this kind produces a continuous stream of operating data from thousands of sites: equipment performance, energy generated and stored, computing capacity delivered to AI inference providers, and payments owed to participating hosts. Blocksight’s agents are expected to ingest that data, reconcile it against the financing structure and provide investors with reporting on the underlying assets through OpenWorld Enterprise. Transaction Status The term sheets with BeyondAI and Meridian are non-binding, except for the provisions expressly stated to be binding, and each proposed transaction remains subject to the completion of confirmatory due diligence, negotiation and execution of definitive documentation, satisfaction of applicable conditions and completion of the contemplated transaction. In addition, the acquisition of Blocksight remains subject to the satisfaction or waiver of customary closing conditions. There can be no assurance that any of these transactions will be consummated on the terms described or at all. articles.title: RBA’s Kent says neutral rate is rising, questions if policy is restrictive enough
articles.description: Kent’s remarks pull in two directions, which may limit any lasting move in the Australian dollar. Endorsing the post-jobs repricing suggests the RBA is comfortable with markets scaling back near-term hike bets, a mild negative for the currency and supportive for short-end bonds. But the neutral rate argument is a hawkish undercurrent, since it implies the 4.60% cash rate may be doing less work than assumed. That makes the 28 October inflation data the pivotal event: a hot print would revive November hike pricing quickly, while a soft one would likely cement a pause. Rate-sensitive sectors, especially property and banks, will be tracking that shift closely. --- Earlier: Euro slides against Australian dollar as three European headwinds hit early trade ---Kent is happy for markets to pare November hike bets after a weak jobs report, but his warning that neutral rates are rising leaves the RBA plenty of room to tighten again if inflation runs hot. Summary: RBA Assistant Governor (Financial Markets) Christopher Kent said there is reasonable evidence neutral rates are rising in Australia and abroad He is confident policy is somewhat restrictive but questioned whether it is restrictive enough Household demand is softening, business credit remains strong, and housing tax changes have helped monetary policy Kent is cautious on monthly jobs data but said the labour market has become less tight He said the market move after last week’s weak jobs report, a lower Australian dollar, lower short-term rates and reduced near-term hike odds, made sense The cash rate is 4.60% after four hikes this year; Q3 CPI is due 28 October, ahead of the 2 to 3 November RBA meeting Reserve Bank of Australia Assistant Governor Christopher Kent said there is reasonable evidence that neutral interest rates are rising, both in Australia and overseas, raising the question of whether monetary policy is as tight as it appears, even after four rate increases this year. Speaking at a fireside chat at the Commonwealth Bank’s Global Markets Conference in Sydney, Kent, who oversees financial markets at the central bank, said he was confident policy is somewhat restrictive but questioned whether it is restrictive enough. The neutral rate is the level of interest rates that neither stimulates nor restrains the economy. If it has drifted higher, a cash rate that looks tight on paper may be exerting less pressure on demand and inflation than policymakers had assumed, which would strengthen the case for keeping rates higher for longer or tightening further. Kent’s remarks come as the RBA weighs its next move. The board lifted the cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.60% on 29 September, its fourth increase of 2026, citing inflation that remains too high, energy prices pushed up by the broadening conflict in the Middle East, and lingering capacity pressures. It said further increases were possible if needed. On the economy, Kent said household demand is softening, while business credit growth remains strong. He described recent tax changes affecting housing as helpful for monetary policy, a sign the bank sees fiscal settings working with it rather than against it on housing demand. He was more cautious on the labour market. Kent said he was wary of reading too much into monthly employment figures, but acknowledged conditions have become less tight. Data last week showed employment fell by about 39,000 in September, against expectations of a gain of around 20,000, with the unemployment rate rising to 4.7%, the highest in around five years. That report sent the Australian dollar and short-term interest rates lower as traders pared bets on a near-term hike. Kent said that market reaction made sense, a comment likely to be read as the bank seeing no reason to push back against the repricing. Even so, the debate is far from settled. ANZ kept its call for a further 25 basis point increase in November after the jobs data, arguing that upward revisions to the bank’s inflation forecasts make a hike more likely than not. The next key test is quarterly inflation data on 28 October, ahead of the RBA’s 2 to 3 November meeting. Kent’s comments on a rising neutral rate suggest that, if inflation surprises to the upside, the bank still sees room to tighten. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: India exports 43% more fuel to the west in Sept: Russian crude a boon for Indian refiners
articles.description: India exports 43% more fuel to the west in Sept: Russian crude a boon for Indian refiners EXC: In September, exports of oil products from Indian refineries to Western nations rose by 43%, reaching 1 billion euros. During this period, refineries in India, Turkey, and Brunei—which process crude oil sourced from Russia—supplied oil products to countries that have imposed sanctions on Russia.

articles.title: “My wages will go over to a local children's charity”: How David Beckham turned his PSG farewell into a charitable pledge
articles.description: David Beckham’s work with UNICEF has covered child health, education, bullying prevention and emergency relief. His 2013 PSG salary pledge supported a local children’s charity, while the 7 Fund backed programmes in several countries. His visits to crisis-hit communities and his use of social media have helped bring public attention to children facing danger, poverty and disrupted education.

articles.description: Indian equities turned around as information technology stocks attracted sustained buying interest. Strong quarterly earnings reports enhanced investor confidence in the market, with the Nifty 50 index achieving a closing point of 23,146, representing a 0.65% rise. Prominent companies like HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank shared their quarterly outcomes, showcasing improved asset quality. Investors are anticipated to keep an eye on upcoming corporate announcements which may guide market trends.
